Due to the departure of a large number of Muslim officials, neither the Assembly nor the Executive Board operated and therefore a Crisis Staff was formed with the task to resolve everyday problems. The Crisis Staff, however, also did not function very well because when the Milici municipality broke away, a number of the Crisis Staff members also moved. Therefore, the Executive Board was reactivated to take over the responsibilities. These issues were further aggravated because the municipality was not able to ask the opinion of the leadership in Sarajevo on many problems because the telephone lines were down and it was not safe to travel by road. Dr. Milenko Stanic does not consider it true that the civilian authorities did not have power and were taken over by the military. Dr. Karadzic never issued him or, as far as he knows, any of the Vlasenica municipality leadership with any order concerning the expulsion of Muslims, the attacks on certain villages, or the carrying out of activities with regard to Muslims. He remembers a speech of Dr. Karadzic held at the funeral of killed combatants of Rogosija. He didn't get an impression there was hatred or call for revenge in that speech. [Interpretation] This would be the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stanic, you were kind enough to bring two documents with you.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: If I may just make an intervention on the text that we have heard. There was an error made in the election results; namely, in the first multi-party elections in Vlasenica in 1990, the Serbian Democratic Party won in Vlasenica. It had more deputies than the Party for Democratic Action, and you read out that we had the same number of deputies. Actually, the SDS had 27, and the SDA had 26 deputies. Our results were better or greater by 600 voters than the results of the SDA. So this is just a correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Stanic. Don't worry, this summary is not an exhibit. Your statement would become an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let us look at 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please be asked to repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D07235. We have to place the document on the ELMO, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stanic, you mentioned in your statement that passes were required for free passage through the territory and at various check-points. You kindly brought copies of these passes. Could you please tell us what these passes are.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: These passes could assist the citizens. Of course their value was different, but the citizens themselves pressured not only the local authorities but other organs, the public security stations, the military, to be issued with some kind of document, because they felt that with a document they could move more safely. So in that sense, the local community in Vlasenica issued certain passes at the request of the citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we activate the ELMO, please, because that's where the translation is. Here we can actually remove one page on one side, because both documents being shown right now on the monitor are identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us what we are seeing, these copies of the passes.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The passes were issued to all citizens of all ethnic groups, and I, as the president of the Assembly and later as the minister in the government, had a certain number of passes. Here we're in -- have the opportunity to see a pass issued by the Sekovici military post. Then there's a special pass from 1992. It's in my name. Then we have two passes issued by the ministry. Actually, three passes issued by the Ministry of Defence, also in my name. This is the period when I was working in the Government of Republika Srpska. And then we see a pass from an enterprise or from the Government of Republika Srpska to be able to enter the Famos premises freely, which is where the government was located at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the translation on the ELMO, please. I cannot see the ELMO on my monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stanic, are you able to explain to us why you needed these passes as the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Because at the time, there were many different check-points held either by the military forces, mostly the police forces. They acted in different ways while monitoring movement. So this pass provided the possibility of passing through these checks without any problem. Some of these passes I used in order to go across the border when I was travelling to the territory of other states. First of all, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document. We do have a translation, but we cannot upload it, it seems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2984, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I now ask for 1D07236 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you explain what this document means? Unfortunately, we still don't have a translation for this, but you'll be able to explain. It's mostly the names. Could you just read the title and the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a list of persons eligible for the exchange of houses and apartments. Owners of apartments and houses who wanted to exchange with refugees from Kladanj, Olovo, Sarajevo, Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they do this under some pressure, and at what time did they arrive at the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The municipal service in charge of issuing passes required all citizens who wanted to travel somewhere to state for what reason they wished to do so. The municipal service did not have information that anybody was doing this under coercion. In exchanges of residences, there would be involved families, Serb families and Muslim families whose representatives would come to the municipal service in charge of these affairs. The service would accept their applications, record them. It would run checks at the public security stations to make sure that these contracts were done properly, whether they were signed under coercion or some other suspect circumstances, and after these checks were completed, the municipal service gave approvals and organised transportation for these citizens depending on where they wished to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we see page 2, and then I'll ask you to read the handwritten portion and explain it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the second part of the check carried out by the competent public security station. It says: "On the part of the public security station of Vlasenica, there are no legal obstacles for the exchange of apartments and houses of the aforesaid persons. The above-said are persons do not feature in the operative records of the Public Security Station Vlasenica. Signed by authorised officer, Stanisic, L."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D2985, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions for Dr. Stanic at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably the number should be MFI D2985.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour, D2985.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stanic, as you have noted, your evidence in this case -- your evidence in chief has been admitted in most part in writing in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you will be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Yes, Ms. Sutherland, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, in paragraph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, in paragraph 13 of your statement you said that on the 26th of December, 1991, the Serbs in the local parliament proposed that a decision be adopted that Vlasenica join the Birac Autonomous District. Just to be clear, you mean the Serbian Autonomous District, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: No, that's not right. It's not the Serbian Autonomous District. It was the Autonomous District of Birac. This term "autonomous district" was accepted at the proposal of Serbian opposition deputies to the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica. It was the condition for voting in favour of this document and for obtaining the majority for the full-fledged decision of 31 deputies. It was their condition that it be called Autonomous District of Birac instead of Serbian Autonomous District. We had a number of Bosniak deputies --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So, Mr. Stanic, this was after the Republika Srpska Assembly passed a decision on the 21st of November, 1991, verifying the declared Serbian autonomous provinces in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which included the Serbian Autonomous Region Romanija-Birac, which comprised of the municipalities of Han Pijesak, Pale, Sokolac, Vlasenica, and Sekovici, as well as the parts of this region's other municipalities with Serbian majority. Is that what you're saying? It was after this decision?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's Exhibit D0083, Your Honours, at English page 33 and B/C/S pages 33 and 34.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask if Dr. Stanic has his statement before him and whether he's able to use it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have my statement here, but I don't understand the question, the regional districts of Han Sokolac, Han Pijesak. How is Vlasenica and Sekovici connected with these areas?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I would have to see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, the -- you said that it was called the autonomous district, and I said to you was that after the Republika Srpska Assembly issued the decision verifying the Serbian autonomous provinces in Bosnia-Herzegovina? And then I made reference to the Serbian Autonomous Region Romanija-Birac. But my question is simply: Was what you were talking about earlier after this decision?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the date. I know we adopted this decision towards the end of December, and the exact date is in my statement, the 26th of December. I don't know when the decision was adopted by the National Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It was on the 21st of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can have MFI P06112, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, this is minutes of a -- minutes of the 2nd Assembly -- 2nd session of the Assembly of the Autonomous District Birac. We see in English and B/C/S page 2, under point 1, it refers to you as president of the executive -- the English translation says "Executive Board," but I think you would agree a better word -- a better translation is president of the Executive Council of the Autonomous District Birac. And again if we can look at -- and you explained a proposal there under point 1. If I can now take you to page -- English page 5 and B/C/S page 4. And under point 2 it says the president -- in the English translation it says, "President of the Autonomous District Assembly Milenko Stanic said," and then you go on. I think you would agree a better translation is president of the Executive Council of the Assembly of the Autonomous District. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Assembly had its organs including the Assembly, the Executive Council and Assembly commissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you were the president of the Executive Council?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was president of the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you recall saying -- making these two points, 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I can't see points 1 and 2. I don't know what you mean. I see proposal number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We see point 2 -- you see point 2. You recall you said to the present parties that you considered that -- that candidates to be proposed to the Executive Council. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was standard procedure. Since the Assembly was made up of deputies from all the Assemblies, it was naturally their demand that from every municipality there would be one representative in the Executive Board or the Executive Council. Otherwise, you could not make a proper structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stanic, under point 1, if we can just quickly go back to page 2 of the B/C/S, you explain the proposal of the operational programme of the Executive Council. You remember doing that? That was discussed at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I think that Assembly session did not adopt a programme --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. You discussed it. You discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I know we agreed that upon the establishment of the Executive Council, we would in that composition draft a programme and verify it at the next session which, however, was not held. So at this Assembly session we did not discuss the programme. It is possible that the introduction which covers proposals by various nominees, we touched upon some issues on which we would work in the future, but the programme was not drafted then, and it was not adopted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document, Your Honour, lift the MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The reason for having put this document marked for identification was because of the provenance. It's an excerpt from some book.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you not -- ready to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's an excerpt from Naser Oric's book, and it has been exhibited in two previous trials, and I actually advised the Chamber of that at the very end of the session last Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We don't have any objection to that portion. We would also appreciate being advised of the provenance when the Prosecution advises the Chamber, because we hadn't been advised until hearing it right now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll admit it in full. So it will be recorded as fully admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, you also chaired a session of the Executive Council of the Birac Serbian Autonomous District held on the 18th of February, 1992, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Right now I can't remember the date unless you show me a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P06113.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, you say -- see here this is a Cyrillic document, and it states it's the minutes of the 1st session of the Executive Council of the Birac SAO, which stands for Serbian Autonomous District, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: That's what it should stand for, but obviously the recording secretary did not pay enough attention to these terms such as "autonomous district." It's true some other municipalities took different decisions than the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You also presented yourself as the president of the Serbian Autonomous District Birac government to the main Belgrade daily, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter number 24620. And I'm sorry, Your Honour, we don't have a translation at the moment, but -- oh, yes, we do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's the article in the top right-hand corner. It's entitled "Overnight to Serbia," published in "Politika" on the 5th of March, 1992, page 8 of the newspaper. It's talking about tensions in Zvornik and Vlasenica, and you're quoted as saying -- you make a statement about the possible proclamation of the independent BiH, and you say: "In case of proclamation of the independent BiH, it is sure that we will not allow any of its laws or regulations to enter in the Serb houses." And you're introduced there as the president or prime minister of the SAO Birac government. So again we're talking about the Serbian SAO. Do you -- you said that, that you wouldn't allow any laws or regulations to enter into the Serb houses in relation to the independent BiH?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Reporters have their own way of reporting. As for representation, they put such elements into their reports, but as far as my position is concerned, it was a bit different than you are presenting it. My position was that I repeated several times --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you -- did you say what you're quoted as being said in this article?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: In that context that you are presenting, no, but I did say that the laws of a sovereign centralised Bosnia-Herzegovina -- or, rather, the laws of Alija's Bosnia-Herzegovina would not be accepted in Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we're admitting only that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That portion, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just in case, do we know who wrote it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you read the journalist's name at the end of the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At the bottom of the article, Mr. Stanic, do you see in Cyrillic who the author of the article is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some person named Pejak [phoen]. I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask distinguished Madam Sutherland to clarify whether Dr. Stanic called himself the president of the SAO government or it was the reporter who added that qualification, because the question implies that Dr. Stanic introduced himself as such, and I don't see it from the article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I think -- he answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6136, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stanic, the Serbian Autonomous District of Birac was a functioning body and did issue proclamations and decisions, did it not? Even as late as late April 1992 it was functioning?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I really don't remember until when it was functioning, but it was not for long. We made a proclamation at the first founding Assembly session in Sekovici, and I believe we did not have more than two sessions of the Executive Council of the region where we discussed mainly economic issues, and another topic was setting up a delegation from that area that would, together with representatives of the Assembly of the Serbian Republic, put forward suggestions in future talks -- or, rather, talks that were already underway on the internal organisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Stanic, you're basically saying you don't really remember until when it was functioning, but it was not for long. I want to show you a document now that --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- that's Exhibit P02615. Now, this is a document from the, again, Serbian Autonomous District of Birac. It's issued by the Crisis Staff in Sekovici on the 29th of April, 1992. And it says: "Pursuant to the decision of the Council for National Security of the Serbian Republic of BH on general mobilisation and on the basis of the estimates of the Crisis Staff of the SAO of Birac on the threat of war, especially in the municipalities of Bratunac and Srebrenica, the Crisis Staff of the SAO Birac hereby brings the following decision," and then proclaiming a state of war. But it's not just --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. This is not an enactment of the Executive Council, and it's not even signed by the Executive Council. It's a document from Sekovici originating from I don't know which organ. I don't know who drafted it. In any case, it's not a document of the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But it's a document issued by the Serbian Autonomous District of Birac, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: No. No. We did not discuss such issues. Of course there were certain members of the Executive Council who tried to abuse their position, mainly in commerce, especially the representative from Sekovici, and that is one of the reasons why we terminated our activities very soon. It's possible that one of these representatives wrote the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we can see the stamp at the top corner. It's been received by the Bratunac Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The point is -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The point is that the Executive Council did not have its Crisis Staff and could not have produced such a document. The Executive Council held only two sessions, stopped working shortly afterwards and there was no Crisis Staff at the level of the region.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. I want to turn now to the Crisis Staff at the municipal level. You state in paragraph 30 that you don't recall the 4th of April, 1992, decision establishing the Vlasenica Crisis Staff, appointing you as president of that body.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can quickly look at P06121.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is the decision appointing you as the president. You also said that -- in paragraph 43 of your statement that you state that you're not familiar with the contents of the Variant A and B document. We can see from the predicate language of this document that the Crisis Staff of which you're the president is established pursuant to the instructions of the Main Board of the SDS. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So these instructions of the Main Board were the -- were the Variant A and B -- was the Variant A and B document, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Why did I state that I don't remember this document? Could you scroll down a little so I can see the stamp. It is evident that this decision was adopted by the Municipal Board, and it was not signed by the president of the Municipal Board, Tomislav Savkic. Another problem is the stamp is not the stamp of the Serbian Democratic Party. It is a stamp of a certain secretariat or a service or a department within the Municipal Assembly. Those were the reasons why I don't remember such document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You were president of the Vlasenica Crisis Staff, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: This Crisis Staff was the Crisis Staff of the SDS. The Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly was established according to different principles based on the statute of the Municipal Assembly and the then laws. It was basically a continuation of the work of an earlier Council for National Security. I think that was its name. That was the name of the municipal body which dealt with extraordinary situations when the Municipal Assembly was unable to sit. I do not recall that these ten people ever met as a group in order to come to certain decisions. The election of a president is up to those who are nominated, and the members were supposed to choose the president amongst themselves. I was the president of the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: And not of the party Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, what -- what instructions, Main Board instructions, are being referred to in -- in the predicate paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you show the top part of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Based on the instruction of the Main Board of the SDS of Bosnia-Herzegovina regarding operations under conditions of imminent threat of war, the Municipal Board of the Vlasenica Municipality SDS at a session on 4 April 1992 made the following decision ..." Whoever drafted this document or whoever certified this document invoked some documents which served as the basis. I am not familiar with the basis of this decision. I'm simply not aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You've never seen the instructions from the Main Board. Is that -- is that your testimony? The instructions that were issued in late December 1991. It's your testimony that you've never seen those instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: What I said is that I do not remember whether I read the instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. I do not recall whether I was in attendance --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay, well --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: -- at the Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Even if you didn't read the instructions, you knew about the contents.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard of those documents, but as for the contents, well, partially perhaps. I heard people discuss it, and they must have touched upon the contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that was to take over the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: You see, throughout 1992 there were constant problems in communication between --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Mr. Stanic, sorry. I'm talking about --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: -- the local bodies of authority and --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm talking about before the war, before the conflict started. I'm talking about in late 1991, early 1992. These instructions that you've just told us about that you heard about, that people told you about, and you said that you must have -- it was -- it was -- they -- they must have touched upon the contents. I'm talking about the document that instructed the Serb -- the SDS parties in the municipalities to form Assemblies to take over the municipalities. That's what I'm referring to when I'm talking about the instructions. And that's what you're referring to, aren't you, when you say that people talked to you about the contents of these documents, these instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: It wasn't me but the person drafting the document. At the time I was very busy in the Municipal Assembly building. The party was run by a different leadership. I didn't have much time for party matters. There was enough on my hands in the Municipal Assembly. Well, I suppose they invoked a certain document when adopting this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, you were a member of the SDS in -- in 1991 and 1992, were you -- were you not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was the first person on the SDS list for the Municipal Assembly in Vlasenica, and I was also the Assembly speaker. I attended the sessions of the Municipal Board when they sat. I do not recall this date, the 4th of April, though, and whether I was present then or not and whether that session took place on that date indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you said that this was -- this Crisis Staff was basically a continuation of the work of an earlier Council for National Security. You said that you thought that was its name. Well, if that was its name, why didn't it continue with that name and not call itself the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Council for All People's Defence, and in crisis times it was to be converted into a Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So this Crisis Staff morphed -- morphed into the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Not in entirety. Some of the members were never in attendance. For example, the person at number 8, I don't remember him ever taking part in the work. Some of the members were also killed or mobilised at the beginning of the war. In terms of composition and the number of people, there was a difference between the municipal Crisis Staff and the Council for All People's Defence as compared to the party organs. There were similarities, but there were differences as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 30 you also state that you don't recall the Crisis Staff meeting before the 21st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 24622, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, this is a decision of the Vlasenica municipality Crisis Staff, issued at its meeting of the 19th of April, 1992, and it's a decision on an imminent threat of war. And it endorses the decision of the National Security Council of the Assembly of the Serbian BiH, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I'd like to say this: Of course, during proofing I had occasion to see some of the documents shown to me by the Defence. Generally speaking, I can say that in these decisions there are certain problems in terms of dates. As I have stated in my statement, I stand by it. I think the Crisis Staff began sitting on the 22nd of April, that is to say, after the 21st of April. Quite a few documents produced by the Crisis Staff were drafted in the secretariat department of the Municipal Assembly. I wasn't in that building where the municipal secretariat was. I was in the administration building of the bauxite mine, which is some 200 metres away from the municipal building. The Executive Board president and I went there after the division of municipality was verified, when the municipality was divided into three parts and the Serbian municipality was established. Now, why they pre-dated these dates is something I don't know. We discussed that issue as well, I believe, on the 22nd rather than on the 19th. I also noticed that a decision of the 30th of March also has certain difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When were you --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: There's another problem here which is the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We will get to that decision. The stamp is the stamp of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica, isn't it? In the republic of Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- Herzegovina. It's the old stamp.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: It is the old stamp, and I think it was kept in the secretariat of the Municipal Assembly, which is in the old Assembly building, and of course this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 23116, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we give the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6137, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Stanic, this is pursuant to a decision of the Crisis Staff at its sitting on the 19th of April, 1992, a decision to disarm the active and reserve forces of the Vlasenica SJB?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is nonsense. This is not a document of the Crisis Staff. The stamp is not that of the Crisis Staff, nor is the signature. We didn't even discuss this decision. I believe this document was planted by some services. There was no need to adopt such a decision. On the 21st of April, in the public security station, there were practically no policemen. I know the chief of the station complained, saying that he would -- he was only able to keep the duty policemen on duty. There was no need for this. There must have been previous calls to have illegal weapons handed over, but I see no reason why a decision of this kind would be issued pertaining to the public security station. The Crisis Staff did not make such decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek this tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We don't have any objection, although I think there's some question as to the validity of the document, but I think that goes to the weight as opposed to its admissibility, so we don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your position about authenticity, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- I'm assuming that the OTP located this when conducting its investigations, and so I don't question the fact that they found it somewhere among the offices in Republika Srpska or in its subsidiary bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this -- this document was provided by the chief of the SJB in Vlasenica. Provided it the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in 2009, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6138, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P03214, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, again this is the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica, a decision to take over power in the area over the municipality of Vlasenica, and the signature block is "President of the Crisis Staff, Mr. Milenko Stanic." So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's -- let's wait until we see that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it also has a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. And it is significantly different from the previous stamp. This is exactly what I was talking about. The date is the 19th of April, which is incorrect. I think it was the 22nd of April. It is not signed. I do not recall if we issued a document like this, but the date is definitely incorrect. It must have been after the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: You see what the problem is --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The problem is this document is before the take-over. You -- the take-over occurred on the 20th, 21st of April, 1992, and this document deciding to take over the power precedes the take-over, does it not? So it would be a bit silly to issue a decision after the take-over on the 22nd of April, as you say, when the take-over occurred before. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I said already. After the army came into the town itself on the 21st, we started with our first session around the 22nd. Now, why we see decisions dated the 19th --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, can I just interrupt you. It says -- under point number 1 it says: "The Vlasenica municipality Crisis Staff hereby adopts the decision to take over power ..." not as you're saying if -- if this had occurred on the 22nd of April, it would have said the Vlasenica municipality Crisis Staff power has been taken over already. This is prior to the take-over.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I see no reason for adopting such a decision. We were the elected authority immediately after the Serb municipality of Vlasenica was established on the 30th [as interpreted] of April when the joint session was held. The Serb deputies remained and elected their people to the bodies and organs. We started setting up our own organs on the 13th of April, but the Crisis Staff was only established after the take-over and, for some reasons of their own, the date was pre-dated by some municipal services.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But, Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The accused overlapped. Could he please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Please do not overlap. Just a second. Let me check that. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 16, it seemed that the witness said the 30th, whereas he said the 13th of April. It is very similar the way it sounds in our language. Could that be checked?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You did say the 13th, didn't you, Mr. Stanic, the 13th of April? But --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- but in fact -- but in fact --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: -- after the joint session of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland. Ms. Sutherland, do you hear in English or in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In English, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please do not overlap with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, but that's not right, is it, because on -- you didn't set up the Serbian Assembly on the 13th of April, did you? That was set up earlier than that. It was actually set up on the 30th of March, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I said during the introductory part that I had insight into some of the documents given by Defence. Some documents bear the date of the 19th of April, which was the session of the Crisis Staff which didn't take place, and the 30th of March when the Assembly did not sit. A session of the Serbian Assembly was held immediately after the joint session on the 14th of April, when we adopted a decision on the division of the municipality into three new municipalities --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: -- the Serbian deputies remained in the Assembly and adopted certain decisions on the appointment of officials. So that date, too, is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter number 24621, please. Now, Your Honour, we may not have a translation for this at the moment. It's being -- it's being done as we speak. Oh, here it is. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, here it says during the session of the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica on the 30th of March, 1992, a decision to appoint you as president, and it's signed by Cedo Vrzina.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Cedo Vrzina. He was the Municipal Assembly secretary, and he was not supposed to sign such documents. The appointment of the municipal president is signed by the speaker Assembly himself, and he was not in that position. In his department is where the documents were created with the wrong dates. I am certain after 22 years that on the 13th of April, the 1st session of the Serb Municipality of Vlasenica Assembly was held following the joint session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P6139, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stanic, you -- the Serbian authorities did then take over power in the days following the 19th of April, 1992, and it was taken over by the --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The forces of the JNA and the formed unit co-ordinated by the SDS Crisis Staff. And this is contained in a report of the 1st Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade commanded by Mile Kosoric. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, P02636. If we can bring that up quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, this is dated the 19th of December, 1994, with reference back to what occurred on the 20th of April, 1992. Now, I note in paragraph 23 of your statement that you say "he claimed," I presume the person you're talking about by "he" is Mile Kosoric, and you are in fact referring to this document, were you not, in paragraph 23 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I did not invoke this document. I wasn't even aware of it. I can't invoke fake documents. You say paragraph 23? Let me have a look. As regards the document, it is true that it was signed for Mile Kosoric. I have to say that this person throughout 1992 was in the theatre of war in Croatia. So he was not in Vlasenica until I joined the government, which was on the 1st of February, 1993. I think it was in late 1993 that Mile Kosoric came to the Vlasenica brigade command. Now, how can a person who was in Croatia could write about Vlasenica events is something that I'm not clear about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see -- well, I don't have that in paragraph 23, any of what was said, in the 23rd paragraph of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does it not start with "he claimed that" --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "He claimed that on the 21st of April, 1992, the Serbs in Vlasenica carried out an armed attack on Vlasenica and captured the town."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So whose document are you talking about there? Where you say "he claimed," are you talking about Kosoric or are you talking about someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, in my original there's none of it, or in the English translation. Whose statement is it then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Let us upload witness's statement, para 23, both in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This was a paragraph that was added to your statement on -- to your previous draft statement, so it must have been something that you said when you signed your statement the other day, on the 16th of February, 2013. So, what document were you referring to in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you see the passage "he claimed that"? I don't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This -- this doesn't appear to be the final version of the witness statement. The document that I received on -- after the 16th had a number of track changes, words added, and this entire paragraph has been added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. In my hard copy I see the passage, but I don't see it here. Let's check how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, what time were you minded to break for lunch?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll break now, then. Let's sort it in the meantime, sort it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is the problem of -- of having a lot of revised statements. Judge Lattanzi's version is different from mine in hard copy, so we'll -- let's sort it out. We'll take a break for 45 minutes and resume at 17 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, I wonder if the matter has been sorted out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it has been sorted out. What happened was that Ms. Sutherland was looking at the track changes version and it was highlighted, and so she believed that it was still included in the statement but, in fact, that was a deletion from the original statement. So that's the problem. But in e-court and what was e-mailed to the parties over the weekend is the final revised statement that everyone should have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When was the last notification filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: The notification itself was filed on Monday. The statement was e-mailed on Saturday evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, we'll leave it then. Among the Judges, it is only Judge Lattanzi that had the correct latest version. Thanks to her efficient, diligent and committed assistant. Well, let's continue then. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I can discuss this with the Defence further, but we also identified a submitted statement that had track changes but did not identify all the deletions. I raise that because I've discussed it with Mr. Robinson, but it occurred to me that we hadn't advised the Court, so perhaps that's something we need to do as well and I can take an opportunity when it presents itself to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please bear in this mind and please do your utmost. Yes. Let's continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, the document that we had on the screen just before we broke for lunch, P02636, the letter from the commander of the 1st Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade, talked about the take-over by JNA forces and the unit co-ordinated by the SDS Crisis Staff liberating the town of Vlasenica. Do you recall seeing that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I have seen the document now. I can analyse it as such. It's full of important facts. We can go over the document so that I can tell you what is false about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the purposes of the transcript, the witness did not say "lazne ne golazne" [phoen], meaning not important, but "false" matters. I understand the interpreter, but I just want to make the correction. [No interpretation]. [In English] Full of "lazne," false facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Do you confirm that, Mr. Stanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. It's a completely false document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter -- sorry, Exhibit P02636 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, it says in this document that in accordance with the decision of the Crisis Staff, mobilisation of the former TO was carried out. And it also says in paragraph 4 that: "The SDS Crisis Staff commanded and controlled detachments in the field through their established staff command and control of these units until 28 June 1992, when all the units became part of the 1st Bircani Brigade." Now, this is consistent with a decision issued by the Vlasenica Serb Crisis Staff on the 19th of April, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I understand your intention, and I understand what the grounds were to draft [Realtime transcript read in error "demographic"] those ordered documents of the 19th of April. Precisely this letter which is a document written in 1994, as I already said, by a person who came to Vlasenica in late 1993. The Crisis Staff never interfered in military operations. We adhered wholly to the positions of the Government of Republika Srpska of the 26th of April, or, rather, the instructions to the Crisis Staffs which in paragraph 4 state that it was -- the question of command of the armed forces and the police is exclusively in the domain of the professionals in those areas and that Crisis Staffs must not interfere in such affairs. So it is evident here that the document is false in respect of the date as well, indicating that the Crisis Staffs existed on the 26th of April. I think you have a decision on the forming of the commissioner's office for Vlasenica, and I think that was on the 15th of June. In late May --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, sorry to interrupt --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: -- May, the Crisis Staffs ceased to exist --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm talking about a decision. We'll bring it up now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 65 ter 23117, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something about the transcript. Line 12, page 76, Dr. Stanic did not say "demographic those documents," he said "the ordered documents," meaning that they were deliberately fabricated. The way it is now, it makes no sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you confirm that, Mr. Stanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So, Mr. Stanic, we see in front of us this document issued by the Serbian municipality of Vlasenica, the decision on the establishment of the Territorial Defence headquarters. And under point 2, the staff's task is to name and establish territorial units and to manage them.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: This also is one of those false documents made to order. It was not signed by me. It's not a Crisis Staff stamp. We didn't have any need for a decision like this. The Vlasenica TO staff was formed on the 15th of April by an order of the TO commander, Ferid Hodzic, who, pursuant to instructions of the BiH Presidency, carried out a division of the TO staff and the TO armed forces into a Serb and Muslim component; namely, a Serbian TO staff and a Muslim TO staff. I spoke about that in my statement in this annex or addition under number 43.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you recognise whose -- whose signature this is? Can we zoom in, collapsing the B/C/S -- the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I cannot tell. I think somebody tried to sign my own signature. There's no name. This is not my signature. I don't know who it was who tried to sign my name. Probably one of those people who were providing these documents pursuant to requests, a request from someone, so that this false story would receive verification in some way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, in the English translation we see a passage about handwritten part on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you see it in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It should be on the next page, Your Honour 06393730. It appears at the top of the page, yes. And in fact, I see on the English translation it says "MA." It should in fact be "MD." We will have that revised. The person that provided us with the document, the person I referred to earlier that gave us the other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6140, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, the -- the -- there was a combat unit of a couple of -- several hundred people strong which were armed by the SDS and trained by the SDS party, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the SDS did not have officers who could train a party army. A party army did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In late 1991, the SDS party armed this combat unit and it was actually stationed at Milici, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I am aware that that unit existed, and I think I talked or addressed a gathering on the occasion of the establishment of that unit, but the position of the Serbian Democratic Party is known. We wholly supported the Yugoslav People's Army, and we did not form party units. But in any event, we did give our support that the Yugoslav People's Army remains as the common component, and they tried to preserve Yugoslavia. That unit was under the control of the Yugoslav People's Army wholly and not under the control of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to move on to another topic. I will leave that there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I'm just wondering if -- it seems to me that the time of the Prosecution had expired a while ago. Maybe I'm not calculating that correctly. It was one hour for this witness; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we allotted one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. My mistake then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something for the transcript before a new question, if possible. Page 79, line 1. The witness said that he knew that one unit existed, not that unit. [In English] "I am aware that that unit existed" should be "I'm aware that a unit existed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. A unit, one unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit P03240.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: While that's coming up, the Serbian Autonomous District Birac was also involved in the moving out of the non-Serb population, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: No. No, it was not. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So this document here where Major Svetozar Andric says that: "Pursuant to the decision of the Birac SAR government, which regulates the moving out of the Muslim population from the territory of Birac SAR, I hereby order," and then he says, "setting up a camp in Vlasenica, forbidding the passing of any arbitrary decision on the physical liquidation of prisoners, the security organ of the detained shall conduct operative interviews and the president," I think the English translation says "prime minister" but I think a better translation is "the president of Birac SAR is to establish contact urgently regarding negotiations on the exchange of prisoners." Now, firstly, you're the president of the Birac SAR, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: That organ doesn't exist. What do you mean a government? We talked about an Executive Council or an Executive Board half an hour ago. The government did not exist. The Executive Board or, rather, the Executive Council existed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no decision of this kind. I've already said that we held two meetings. We discussed some questions, not these questions, and you can see in item 4 of this decision that I am being ordered to, but how can anybody order me as the president of the municipality to do something?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the rest what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably you were too fast. The interpreters couldn't hear the last part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 4 of this order saying that the president of the government of Birac should immediately contact -- so any -- nobody can order a representative of a civilian government what to do. So this indicates that this decision has a lot of errors. Nobody from our board reviewed these questions according to the statute or the regulations that we were supposed to review, did not -- it was not provided for that we review these questions, that we deal with them in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So you're talking about the board that you say doesn't exist didn't have to review these --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The government did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can I have Exhibit P06030, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a "Javnost" article of the 6th of June, 1992. So when they make reference to the decision made by the government of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Birac, that didn't -- you're saying that this newspaper must be wrong as well?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I am seeing this document for the first time. I would need to review it in detail. "Javnost" is – whose magazine is that, what is the source of this information? If we have time, I can...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's a very short article, Mr. Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Let me look at it, please. Only the first part could be accepted, that we discussed a delegation which, with the president of the National Assembly, would establish the positions in future negotiations about the structure of Bosnia and Herzegovina. These other articles relating to safe moving in and moving out, this is probably the position of the journalist who reported on the events in his own way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I will leave that there and move on to another topic given the time. In paragraph 27 of your statement, you said that when the military operations started in the villages around Vlasenica, a large number of Muslims poured into Vlasenica from these villages. And you said that the majority of them were housed in the "holding centre" in Susica. By "holding centre," do you mean where Muslims were detained?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about military operations here. These were areas where conflicts broke out between the warring parties. These are --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic if I can --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: -- suburban neighbourhoods of Vlasenica --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can interrupt you. If -- in relation to the words "holding centre," did you mean the place where the Muslims were detained? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I cannot answer in the way that you seek. I would have to explain the situation so that the Chamber could understand it and you also --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In paragraph 27 --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: -- so when we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Stanic. In paragraph 27 you say a large number of Muslims poured into Vlasenica, and then you said that the majority of them, i.e., the Muslims, were housed in the holding centre. And I asked you, simply, does the "holding centre" mean where these Muslims were detained in -- in Susica? In Susica camp.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes. The correct name of that paragraph is that a part of this population who had property in the town, houses and apartments, were accommodated in their own houses and apartments, and that other part from the rural area, they were placed in the collection centre by the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And why -- why do you refer to them then as prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Who's talking about prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'll show you a document in a moment where you refer to them as prisoners. Why do you refer to them as prisoners if they were in a holding centre or collection centre? Okay, let me -- let me -- let me ask you another question. You said that you didn't know about what was going on in this TO building in Susica -- Susica, where persons were being housed, but you're being economical with that statement, aren't you, because you did know about these people, and you did know about the number of people that were being held there.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: I do have a paragraph here which I clarify that situation. I said what I knew, how the collection centre was formed and why we knew it was a collection centre, but it was under the control. These were military facilities, so I cannot talk about some things that I don't know. I cannot accept whatever anything says and create false documents here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In paragraph 33 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the record, the paragraph you referred to seems to be to para 26, not 27, in the latest version.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, that would be right, Your Honour, if this other paragraph is -- that didn't have the strike-through is deleted, yes. You're correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, in paragraph of what is now 32, you said that -- or in the paragraph that you talk about in your statement where you say that after the war commissioners were appointed on the 16th of June, 1992, and that's actually an exhibit in our case, P05399, which was a document signed by you, your function was basically to co-operate with the War Commission and municipality Assembly deputies who were not militarily engaged, and you said that this work bore mostly a humanitarian character. You say that, Mr. Stanic, but in reality you were involved in matters relating to the army as well, and after the commissioners had been appointed you met with high-level personnel from the military and the police about issues relating to soldiers and detention facilities, didn't you? Yes or no? You met with high-level personnel from the military and police about issues relating to soldiers and detention facilities? Mr. Stanic, did you --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me. When you say "high-ranking officers," you need to tell me specifically what you're referring to in order for me to be able to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. I'll show you -- I will show you General Ratko Mladic's notebook.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have P01478. If we could go to the entry for the 25th of June, 1992, which is e-court page 227 and in the B/C/S it's 226. Just so that we can see the date of the 25th of June, 1992. It must be -- we see here -- on the English we see the 25th of June. If we could perhaps go one more in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, you spoke at this meeting --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we go one more page further of the B/C/S, please. Okay. We will go to where Mr. Stanic is talking. It's -- it's on page 232 of e-court and page 231 in B/C/S. Okay. It must be -- it must be page 232 of the actual document, so if we can go forward six pages, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: English e-court page number 232.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see on the screen at the moment, Your Honour, it's got 226 at the very top. That's the actual page of the -- the -- of the notebook. So I think if we go to page 232 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, I see 229 with it, but e-court page 232. I'm seeing president of the SAO Milenko Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So whatever page -- I'm sorry, what page is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, and it's 231 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we upload English page 23 -- yes, and I think two pages before in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, it states here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It states here, Mr. Stanic, at this meeting which was held on the 25th of June with representatives of the Vlasenica civilian police and military authorities, that you stated here a large number said they wanted to move away. Over 800 prisoners, 200 of whom are women and children who were brought last night pose a problem. And then you're also talking about the number of soldiers who have been mobilised. Now, this is what I'm talking about, a high-level meeting that you attended?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is one of General Mladic's notebooks. I think that many of these things -- well, I didn't have such information. I couldn't discuss such facts, especially the number of mobilised soldiers and pieces of weapons. As regards prisoners, we did stress the problem of the high school centre, and we addressed the Main Staff with it because the school had been closed down. The principal of the high school asked that classrooms be provided for him to get them ready for the next school year, and we kept asking the Main Staff to provide appropriate facilities so that we could ensure the functioning of the high school centre in Vlasenica. And we can only discuss this issue within that framework. I suppose that this note was made by someone from the Secretariat of Defence or of the TO. I don't know if the General himself signed underneath these entries.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, 230 in the English. We see that Major Slobodan Pajic talks about a battalion was formed. Can we please go to the next page. Down the bottom it says Major Slobodan Pajic, and over onto the following page, the manpower was earlier armed through parties and they were approximately 600 men in territorial based units. So -- and then lists the number of weapons that they have. Then we also have over on page 232, so the following page, we have the chairman of the Municipal Assembly Bozo Milic, who talks about we have 270 empty apartments and 250 houses. So all this is being discussed at a high level with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's not the only the meeting that you attended, is it, Mr. Stanic? You also attended a meeting on the 30th of June, 1992, at Zvornik with Karadzic, Mladic, Captain Dragan, and around 20 civilian and military officials from East Bosnia municipalities. Do you remember attending that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: As I said in my statement, in 1992 I met with Dr. Karadzic twice, and I also had in mind this particular meeting in Zvornik, and we greeted each other when he addressed those who attended the funeral of those who were killed in Rogosija.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You -- and the meeting in -- for Zvornik is in this same Exhibit P01478, and you were speaking, you were the second person to brief Mr. Karadzic and General Mladic. And that's at e-court page 248 of the English and 246, 247 of the B/C/S. And one of the topics discussed at that meeting was the expulsion of Muslims. Mr. Stanic, you were -- on another topic, if I can direct your attention now to the sale of war booty. You were aware of that occurring, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I think that the witness ought to be given an opportunity to comment on what's in e-court recorded at that meeting or else the Prosecution shouldn't even be referring to it. It's not proper to refer to something and then just move on without giving the witness a chance to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's show him the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, do you know what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we're still on the Mladic diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I attended the meeting in Zvornik. Now, what the General wrote into his notebook concerning that meeting is something I am unaware of. I can have a look certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May we go to page -- sorry, Your Honour. I've been advised I'm officially out of time, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we can go to page 248 of the English translation, another two pages on, please. Perhaps we can try page -- it's -- I'm sorry, 245 of the notebook. So where we have -- so we need to go back three pages. I'm sorry, it's actually e-court page 248. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see down the bottom: "Mr. Stanic, President of Vlasenica Municipal Assembly. "We have defined the western boundaries in the area of the Birac region." And it's in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, we haven't yet had the proper page in --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm trying to -- I'm trying to find -- there it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see down the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So we're actually on the -- on the meeting in Zvornik on the 30th of June, 1992. But I'll take you to the page where the matter of expelling of the Muslims and that was Marko Pavlovic speaking at page 250 of the notebook, which is in e-court page 251, 252.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if we go over the page, please. And again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So down the bottom of this page 250: "We were most active in evicting the Muslims." We had -- and over the page -- "we had brought peace to Sepak, Divic and Kozluk. Some of them wanted to move out while we demanded it. We had to evict some of the people also for the sake of our 'heroes' who fled from Kovacevici." So that was the reference that I was referring to when I said that expulsions of Muslims were discussed at this meeting that you attended.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, do I have time to show the witness two more documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question with respect to this diary at all?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, my -- my -- I was -- I took Mr. Stanic to the entries of the earlier meeting and then I also said: "That wasn't the only meeting you attended. You also attended a meeting on the 30th of June, 1992, where the topic of the meeting -- one of the topics at the meeting was the expulsion of Muslims." Mr. Robinson then asked for those pages to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what was the witness's answer? I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That he did attend the meeting. He does recall attending this meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what the central issue was at that meeting that I put forward. As for the issue of Zvornik, I am not familiar with it. Marko Pavlovic discussed the situation in Zvornik. The greatest problems for the municipalities of Vlasenica, Bratunac, and Milici at the time was the issue of road travel from Vlasenica to Konjevic Polje to Zvornik. We asked the army to put conditions in place so as to enable unhindered economic activity along that road. I heard that the General wrote down that mopping up was required. It is a military term. In civilian authorities we do not use such parlance. We asked that the armed formations in the area should be used to secure the road, since a number of killings had occurred along it, and later on it was completely cut off. So that was our main problem. As regards any other issues, I don't recall having them discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have two very, very brief areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Stanic, I said to you a moment ago that I wanted to turn to the topic of war booty and that you were aware of the sale of this, weren't you? When you were the RS minister of commerce and supplies.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO STANIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a decree which regulated that issue as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 24625, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
